title: Branching, Switching & The HEAD Pointer
description: Understand lightweight branches as movable pointers, inspect the HEAD reference, and switch contexts with git switch.

blocks.content: A branch is an independent line of development. When you create a branch, you get your own workspace where you can make changes without affecting the main code. This is how teams work on multiple features at the same time without stepping on each other.

## Creating and Switching Branches

Create a new branch and switch to it:
```
git switch -c feature/login
```
(The `-c` means "create". Older Git versions use `git checkout -b feature/login`.)

Switch to an existing branch:
```
git switch main
```

List all branches (the `*` marks the current one):
```
git branch
```

## How Branches Work

A branch is just a pointer to a commit. When you commit on a branch, that pointer moves forward. The other branches stay exactly where they were.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["commit 1"] --> B["commit 2"] --> C["commit 3"]
    C --> D["commit 4 - main"]
    C --> E["commit 4 - feature/login"]
    E --> F["commit 5 - feature/login"]
```

In the diagram above, `main` and `feature/login` both started from commit 3 but now have different histories.

## The HEAD Pointer

`HEAD` is a special pointer that always means "where I am right now". When you switch branches, HEAD moves to point at that branch. When you commit, HEAD and the current branch both move forward.

blocks.question: You create a branch called `feature/search` from `main` and make 3 commits on it. What happens to `main`?
options: main automatically picks up the new commits
main stays exactly where it was - the new commits are only on feature/search
main is deleted when you create the new branch
main and feature/search share commits until you merge
blocks.explanation: Creating a branch and committing to it does not affect any other branch. `main` stays at the same commit it was at when you branched off. Your new commits only exist on `feature/search` until you explicitly merge or cherry-pick them.
